t:
(a) 
Section 502(b)(2) of the Housing Act of 1949 is amended by inserting the following before the semicolon at the end thereof: “, except that any prepayment of a loan made or insured under section 514 or 515 shall be subject to the provisions of subsection (c)”.
 
    (b) 
Section 502 of such Act is amended by inserting the following new subsection at the end thereof:


“(c) 

(1) 
Except as provided in paragraph (2), the Secretary may not accept an offer to prepay, or request refinancing in accordance with subsection (b)(3) of, any loan made or insured under section 514 or 515 of this title pursuant to a contract entered into before or after the date of enactment of this subsection, unless the Secretary takes appropriate action which will obligate the borrower (and successors in interest thereof) to utilize the assisted housing and related facilities for the purposes specified in section 514 or 515, as the case may be, for a period of—

“(A) 
fifteen years from the date on which the loan was made in the case of a loan made or insured pursuant to a contract entered into before or after the date of enactment of this subsection and utilized for housing and related facilities which have not received assistance under section 521 (a)(1)(B) or (a)(2) of this title or section 8 of the United States Housing Act of 1937; or


“(B) 
twenty years from the date on which the loan was made in the case of any other such loan;

or until the Secretary determines (prior to the end of such period) that there is no longer a need for such housing and related facilities to be so utilized or that Federal or other financial assistance provided to the residents of such housing will no longer be provided.


“(2) 
In the case of any such loan made or insured pursuant to a contract entered into before the date of enactment of this subsection, the Secretary, after examining an offer to prepay such loan and the likely consequences of accepting such offer, shall accept such offer without taking the appropriate action described in paragraph (1) unless, after such examination, the Secretary determines that—

“(A) 
due to a change in the use of such housing and related facilities, or to an increase in rental or other charges, likely to occur as a result of prepayment, the low and moderate income and elderly tenants occupying the assisted housing and related facilities at the time of such offer cannot reasonably be expected to remain in occupancy for the applicable period described in paragraph (1), but notwithstanding such a determination, the Secretary shall accept such an offer without taking such appropriate action if such tenants who are likely to be displaced as a result of such changes or increases will be provided with affordable, decent, safe, sanitary, and available alternative housing; or 


“(B) 
in the case of housing and related facilities containing more than ten dwelling units, the changes likely to occur as a result of such prepayment will have a substantial, adverse effect on the supply of affordable, decent, safe, and sanitary housing available to low and moderate income and elderly persons in the area in which such housing and related facilities are located.”.

fable.w: The section sets conditions under which the Secretary may accept loan prepayment offers and has the Secretary make those determinations unilaterally. The tempting reading is that the borrower's offer, or the consideration of tenant impacts, brings outside parties into the decision. But an offer to prepay is akin to an application, and tenants are only the subject of the Secretary's findings, not consulted. There is no comment period, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section outlines the conditions under which the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development may accept a loan prepayment from a borrower. The interaction described is a transactional one between a federal agency and a private party regarding a specific loan contract. It does not involve consultation with outside entities, public hearings, advisory boards with non-federal members, or coordination with state/local governments before a policy decision. The 'borrower' is a party to a contract, not a participant in the governmental decision-making process as defined.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary may not accept an offer to prepay... unless the Secretary takes appropriate action which will obligate the borrower

opus.w: The section limits when the Secretary may accept loan prepayments, and the Secretary decides alone after examining the offer and its likely consequences. The borrower's offer to prepay works like an application or request, not participation in a federal decision. Considering tenants' interests is not consulting them. Nothing provides for consultation with outsiders, a public hearing, comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue.

opus.b: The tempting reading is that the borrower's "offer to prepay" brings an outside party into the Secretary's decision, or that weighing the interests of tenants counts as consulting them. Neither holds up. The borrower's offer is the request the Secretary rules on, much like an application, not a say in policy. The Secretary considers tenant welfare on his own and never has to consult them. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the conditions under which the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development may accept a loan prepayment from a borrower. It describes an administrative review process for a specific financial transaction (loan prepayment/refinancing). The definition explicitly states that participation 'does not include applications for benefits or grants.' A request for loan prepayment is analogous to an application for a financial benefit or transaction approval, not a participatory mechanism like a public hearing, advisory committee, or consultation with outside entities on policy. The Secretary's determination is based on statutory criteria, not on required consultation with outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary may not accept an offer to prepay... unless the Secretary takes appropriate action which will obligate the borrower... to utilize the assisted housing... for a period of... fifteen years... or twenty years
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Secretary's examination of the "likely consequences" of prepayment implies a need to consult with tenants or local housing authorities to determine those consequences. However, the text does not explicitly require such consultation; it only requires the Secretary to make a determination based on an examination. The primary interaction described is between the borrower (applying for prepayment) and the Secretary (approving or denying it). This is an administrative decision regarding a specific loan application, not a participatory process involving outside parties in the formulation of policy or decision-making criteria. The definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" (and by extension, loan prepayments/refinancing) from participation.
